citation: PMID:15152005 (Frick et al. 2004 J Biol Chem)
claim_tested: The homologous N-terminal hydrophobic segment of AADAC is an uncleaved anchor that sets lumenal orientation of the catalytic domain
key_finding: Lumenal orientation of 11beta-HSD1 and 50-kDa esterase/arylacetamide deacetylase (E3, AADAC) is determined by their N-terminal transmembrane domains; Glu25/Glu26 (11beta-HSD1) and Asp25 (E3) are a second orientation determinant; Lys4-to-Ile in E3 did not invert topology
context: Human AADAC and HSD11B1 expressed in cells; ER membrane topology and activity assays
confidence_and_limitations: High for AADAC. Indirect for AADACL4: transfer rests on homology and on AADACL4 carrying the equivalent acidic determinant (Glu26/Asp32). No AADACL4 construct was tested.

claim_tested: Current UniProt N-terminal call for AADACL4
key_finding: Topological domain 1-4 cytoplasmic; Transmembrane 5-25 Helical, Signal-anchor for type II membrane protein; Topological domain 26-407 lumenal; all ECO:0000255
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level only. Every N-terminal feature is ECO:0000255 sequence analysis. Protein existence level 3 (inferred from homology).

citation: UniProt P22760 / Q6PIU2 / Q6P093 / Q5VUY0 (database records)
claim_tested: UniProt is internally inconsistent across the AADAC family
key_finding: AADAC and NCEH1 annotated type II signal anchor; AADACL2 annotated cleaved signal peptide 1-18; AADACL3 has no N-terminal feature at all; catalytic registers differ by only 2-4 residues (Ser189/191/193)
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level. Shows the divergent calls track predictor behaviour rather than sequence differences; AADACL2 is the outlier because it carries both AADAC determinants (Lys4
column8: Asp25) yet is called a cleaved SP.

claim_tested: Hydrophobic-segment insertion energetics discriminate the two readings
key_finding: AADACL4 best 19-residue window 6-24 scores -2.61 on the Hessa biological scale, the 0.4th percentile of 738 experimentally verified human signal peptides (median +3.74, 5th pct -0.33) and the ~25th percentile of 316 type II signal anchors. AADAC +1.70, NCEH1 +0.82, AADACL2 +2.28, AADACL3 -2.37
confidence_and_limitations: High within its assumptions. Uses the Hessa centre-position values summed over a 19-residue window as a proxy
column8: not the full positional dG predictor; the published dG predictor server was not accessible.

claim_tested: A calibrated SP-vs-anchor classifier places AADACL4 with the anchors
key_finding: Logistic model on 8 features, 5-fold CV AUC 0.975. P(cleaved SP): AADAC 0.05, AADACL3 0.18, AADACL4 0.22, NCEH1 0.57, AADACL2 0.84. Verified SPs out-of-fold median 0.99 (5th pct 0.58); anchors median 0.05 (95th pct 0.80). Only 1.1% of verified SPs score at or below 0.22
context: Human; 738 SP positives (ECO:0000269) vs 316 type II anchors
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-to-high. The anchor class is annotated ECO:0000255 so the negative class is itself partly computational. NCEH1 at 0.57 is the key calibration point: a protein whose anchor is accepted scores more SP-like than AADACL4.

claim_tested: Cleavage-site P1/P3 residues alone do not refute the SP reading
key_finding: Best architecture-compatible site is after Ala23 with P3 Val21 (context GVFVWA|VFE). Ala is P1 at 340/738 verified sites and Val is P3 at 153/738, so both residues are permissive. The site fails on architecture: full PWM score 6.90 vs verified-site median 11.92 and decoy 95th percentile 6.35; c-region P6-P1 mean Kyte-Doolittle +1.95 vs verified-SP mean +0.58; site offset from the hydrophobic-segment end is -1
confidence_and_limitations: High. This is an explicit partial-negative: the P1/P3 test named in the seed hypothesis is uninformative on its own.

claim_tested: The positive-inside signature discriminates the two readings
key_finding: K+R difference across 15-residue flanks is 0 for AADACL4 (N-flank MAVPW 0, C-flank FEHFLTTDIPATLQH 0), 0 for NCEH1, 0 for AADACL3, +1 for AADAC, -1 for AADACL2. 36/37 AADACL4 orthologs have no cytosolic Lys/Arg
confidence_and_limitations: High. Explicit negative: the positive-inside rule is silent for AADACL4 and for NCEH1. Frick et al. showed the cytosolic Lys is dispensable in AADAC when the acidic determinant is present.

claim_tested: Model architecture matches a type II anchor rather than a cleaved presequence
key_finding: Residues 5-25 form a continuous helix (100% of i,i+4 CA distances within 1.2 A of 6.2 A), mean pLDDT 90.6, CB-neighbour burial 11.8, zero residues within 8 A of the folded domain (110-407), median minimum distance 23.7 A. AADAC and NCEH1 anchors have burial 11.0 and 10.9. Global pLDDT 96.0
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. AlphaFold does not model the membrane
column8: so a detached helix is consistent with an anchor but does not prove non-cleavage. The architecture is identical to the two characterised paralogs.

key_finding: AADACL4 and AADACL3: 2 TM, 0 SP (o6-29i41-60o). AADAC: 2 TM, 0 SP. NCEH1 and AADACL2: 0 TM, signal peptide predicted. The AADACL4 second TM (41-60) has AlphaFold burial 17.4 against a folded-domain mean of 19.8 with 6/20 residues contacting the core, so it is part of the fold
context: Human sequences; Phobius (Kall, Krogh, Sonnhammer, J Mol Biol 338:1027-1036, doi 10.1016/j.jmb.2004.03.016)
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Phobius predicts no signal peptide for AADACL4 but mis-calls NCEH1 as having one
column8: and its AADACL4 second TM is refuted structurally. Generic predictors over-call signal peptides in this family.

claim_tested: The anchor-like signature is conserved, not a human-specific quirk
key_finding: 37 Ensembl 1:1 AADACL4 orthologs (perc_id 45-99%): median dG19 -2.16; 32/37 (86%) below the verified-SP 5th percentile; 28/37 (76%) retain an acidic residue in the first lumenal turn, F-E-H-F at 25-28 in all 9 primates; 36/37 have no cytosolic Lys/Arg
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-to-high. Ortholog classifier scores straddle 0.5 (20/37 below)
column8: so conservation is strong for the energetics and the acidic determinant but weaker for the composite score.

claim_tested: The cleaved-SP reading has a testable consequence that fails
key_finding: Whole-chain 19-residue insertion profile: AADACL4 downstream minimum +4.91 at residue 48, zero windows below 0. Same for all paralogs. Cleavage would therefore release a soluble lumenal or secreted esterase with no membrane anchor
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. The inference that AADACL4 should be membrane-bound comes from its characterised paralogs

claim_tested: Is there any primary literature on the AADACL4 protein?
key_finding: Neither paper studies the protein: a sheep milk-trait selection scan listing AADACL4 among 71 FST-region genes, and a six-gene uterine sarcoma RNA-seq prognostic signature
context: Sheep genome scan; human TCGA uterine sarcoma
confidence_and_limitations: High. Establishes that no experimental topology
column8: localization or enzymology data exist for AADACL4.

claim_tested: Is AADACL4 expressed at a level that supports protein-level curation?
key_finding: No RNA tissue-specificity score; single tissue-specific value 1.7 nTPM in choroid plexus; no subcellular location data
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level. Very low expression weakens the case for asserting any cellular component annotation as established.
